name: p-modeling
description: Design concurrent or retrying code with a P model checked by snappea, then test the real implementation against what the model found.
---

# P modeling

P finds bugs that only appear in some orderings: two clients read the same version,
a retry arrives after the state changed, a step fails between read and write. Use it
for shared state, retries, concurrency and recovery. Pure transformations need only
ordinary tests.

The model is worth what it changes in the code and tests. Follow these steps in order.

## 1. List the risks (before any code)

Write down, in `DESIGN.md`:

- the contract in checkable sentences ("a retried request returns its first result and
  has no further effect");
- the real atomic primitives (one compare-and-swap on one key, a lock, a transaction).
  Everything else can interleave;
- 5-10 concrete scenarios that could break the contract. Always consider:
  two clients that read the same version; a retry after another request changed the
  state (including retries of rejected or empty results); two objects sharing one
  store; each precondition false on its own; values exactly at each boundary.

## 2. Model the algorithm, not the API

- One machine for the store, holding exactly what the real store holds. Its handlers
  are the real primitives: `load` replies with (version, value); `cas` succeeds only at
  the current version.
- Client machines run your algorithm: send load, receive, decide, send cas, retry on
  failure. Every `send`/`receive` is a point where another client can run. If the
  whole operation is one handler, the model assumes the race away.
- A `spec` monitor computes the expected results from the contract and the history of
  requests, independently of the algorithm, and asserts each actual result.
- Drive it with 2-3 clients and small `choose(n)` inputs, plus fixed tests for the
  scenarios from step 1. Start from the [syntax reference](reference/p-patterns.md)
  and [CAS + retries example](examples/cas-retry/Balance.p).

## 3. Check until it passes for real

```sh
snappea check            # every test case, then coverage and mutation checks
```

- Exit 1 is work to do: a bug (fix the design; keep the scenario), a coverage gap
  (add a scenario), or a surviving mutant (an assertion is missing). Read each one.
- Do not finish with `--no-mutation` or `--allow-incomplete-coverage`. Use them only
  while iterating. If search is incomplete, shrink the bounds or raise `--timeout`.
- A bug found here is the payoff: write it down, fix the design, then implement.

## 4. Implement, then test what the model explored

Read [testing the implementation](guides/testing-implementation.md). For each
scenario and each bug the model found, write a Python test that makes it happen on the
real code. Random thread stress rarely hits a race; force it:

- wrap the store so a competing call runs between this call's load and its
  compare-and-swap, or so two calls read the same version before either writes;
- retry a request after another request changed the state, through a second object.

Add an observation test: run real calls, record their actual arguments and results as
events, and check them against your P spec with `snappea.check_events` (install
`pysnappea`, `import snappea`). See [implementation](guides/implementation.md).

## 5. Prove the tests can fail

Break your implementation on purpose, one change at a time (ignore the
compare-and-swap result, drop a retry memo, flip a boundary `<` to `<=`, keep state
in the object instead of the store). Run the tests each time; every break must fail a
test. Add a test for any that pass. Restore the code.

## Done means

- `snappea check` exits 0, with complete search or stated bounds.
- `python -m pytest` passes, including forced-interleaving and observation tests.
- Every hand-made break from step 5 fails a test.
- `DESIGN.md` states the contract, primitives, scenarios, model bounds, what the model
  found, and what is not covered.

## References

- [Syntax and commands](reference/p-patterns.md), [modeling](guides/modeling.md),
  [scenarios and oracles](guides/scenarios-and-oracles.md), [recovery](guides/recovery.md).

# Lock service with fencing tokens

Implement `LockService` and `Resource` in `solution.py`, keeping all state in
`runtime.Store` (see `runtime.py`).

```python
LockService(store, ttl: int)
acquire(client: str, now: int) -> int | None
release(client: str, token: int, now: int) -> bool

Resource(store, name: str)
write(token: int, value: str) -> bool
read() -> str | None
```

- `acquire` grants the lock when no one holds an unexpired lease, and returns a fencing
  token. A lease granted at `now` expires at `now + ttl`; it is expired for any
  `now >= now + ttl`. Tokens are integers that strictly increase over the life of the
  store. If `client` already holds the unexpired lease, `acquire` returns that lease's
  token. Otherwise it returns `None`.
- `release` ends the lease if `client` holds the lease with `token` and it is unexpired at
  `now`, and returns whether it did.
- A `Resource` is protected by fencing: `write` rejects (returns `False`, no effect) a
  token that was never issued, or a token lower than one already used for an accepted
  write to that resource. Otherwise it stores `value` and returns `True`.
- Many `LockService` and `Resource` objects in many threads may share one `Store`; all
  `LockService` objects for a store use the same `ttl`. Callers supply `now`, and calls
  from different clients may arrive with out-of-order times.

Use P to model the design before implementing it, and to test the implementation.
`snappea` and the `pysnappea` Python package are installed. Keep your P files and
tests in this directory; the tests must run with `python -m pytest`.

import threading
import pytest
from snappea import check_events

from runtime import Store
from solution import LockService, Resource


class HookStore:
    """Wraps a Store; one-shot hooks run right after a matching load (before the
    caller decides) so a competitor can interleave between load and CAS."""

    def __init__(self, inner=None):
        self.inner = inner or Store()
        self.after_load = []  # list of (key, fn)
        self.log = []

    def load(self, key):
        result = self.inner.load(key)
        self.log.append(("load", key))
        for i, (k, fn) in enumerate(self.after_load):
            if k == key:
                del self.after_load[i]
                fn()
                break
        return result

    def compare_swap(self, key, version, value):
        self.log.append(("cas", key))
        return self.inner.compare_swap(key, version, value)


def svc(store=None, ttl=3):
    store = store or Store()
    return store, LockService(store, ttl)


# ---- basic contract ----

def test_acquire_release_and_tokens_increase():
    _, a = svc()
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 0)
    assert t1 is not None and t1 >= 1
    assert a.acquire("a", 1) == t1          # holder gets same token back
    assert a.acquire("b", 1) is None
    assert a.release("a", t1, 2) is True
    assert a.release("a", t1, 2) is False   # already released
    t2 = a.acquire("b", 2)
    assert t2 > t1
    assert a.release("b", t2, 2)
    assert a.acquire("a", 2) > t2


def test_expiry_boundary():
    _, a = svc(ttl=3)
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 10)
    assert a.acquire("b", 12) is None       # now < now0+ttl
    t2 = a.acquire("b", 13)                 # now == expiry: expired
    assert t2 is not None and t2 > t1


def test_release_boundary_and_preconditions():
    _, a = svc(ttl=3)
    t = a.acquire("a", 0)
    assert a.release("b", t, 1) is False    # wrong client only
    assert a.release("a", t + 1, 1) is False  # wrong token only
    assert a.release("a", t, 3) is False    # exactly at expiry: too late
    assert a.release("a", t, 2) is True     # one before expiry
    t = a.acquire("a", 5)
    assert a.release("a", t, 8) is False
    assert a.acquire("b", 8) is not None


def test_release_of_expired_does_not_free_a_new_holder():
    _, a = svc(ttl=3)
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 0)
    t2 = a.acquire("b", 3)
    assert a.release("a", t1, 4) is False   # stale token
    assert a.acquire("a", 4) is None        # b still holds
    assert a.release("b", t2, 4) is True


def test_out_of_order_times():
    _, a = svc(ttl=3)
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 10)
    assert a.acquire("b", 5) is None        # unexpired for any now < 13
    assert a.acquire("a", 5) == t1
    t2 = a.acquire("b", 13)
    assert t2 > t1
    assert a.acquire("a", 1) is None        # earlier time cannot take b's lease


def test_tokens_survive_release_and_expiry():
    store, a = svc(ttl=1)
    seen = []
    for i in range(5):
        seen.append(a.acquire("c%d" % (i % 2), i * 2))
        if i % 2:
            a.release("c%d" % (i % 2), seen[-1], i * 2)
    assert seen == sorted(set(seen))
    # a second service object on the same store continues the sequence
    b = LockService(store, 1)
    assert b.acquire("z", 100) > seen[-1]


def test_acquire_retry_after_others_changed_state():
    _, a = svc(ttl=3)
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 0)
    assert a.acquire("a", 1) == t1
    t2 = a.acquire("b", 3)
    assert a.acquire("a", 4) is None        # no stale memo of a's old token
    assert a.acquire("b", 4) == t2


# ---- fencing ----

def test_fencing_rules():
    store, a = svc(ttl=3)
    r = Resource(store, "r")
    assert r.read() is None
    assert r.write(0, "x") is False         # never issued
    assert r.write(1, "x") is False         # not yet issued
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 0)
    t2 = a.acquire("b", 3)
    assert r.write(t2 + 1, "x") is False    # never issued (just above last)
    assert r.write(-1, "x") is False
    assert r.read() is None
    assert r.write(t2, "new") is True
    assert r.write(t1, "old") is False      # lower than used
    assert r.read() == "new"
    assert r.write(t2, "again") is True     # equal token is allowed
    assert r.read() == "again"

    # lock key and resource keys do not collide

    store = HookStore()
    _, a = svc(store)
    results = {}
    barrier = threading.Barrier(2)
    inner_load = store.load
    count = {"n": 0}
    lock = threading.Lock()

    def load(key):
        v = inner_load(key)
        with lock:
            count["n"] += 1
            first_two = count["n"] <= 2
        if first_two:
            barrier.wait(timeout=5)
        return v
    store.load = load

    def run(name):
        results[name] = a.acquire(name, 0)
    ts = [threading.Thread(target=run, args=(n,)) for n in "xy"]
    [t.start() for t in ts]
    [t.join(10) for t in ts]
    assert sorted(v is None for v in results.values()) == [False, True]
    winner = [n for n, v in results.items() if v is not None][0]
    assert a.acquire(winner, 1) == results[winner]


def test_competitor_between_load_and_cas_in_acquire():
    store = HookStore()
    _, a = svc(store)
    other = LockService(store.inner, 3)
    won = {}
    store.after_load.append(("lock", lambda: won.update(t=other.acquire("rival", 0))))
    assert a.acquire("me", 0) is None       # must re-read and re-decide
    assert won["t"] is not None
    assert other.acquire("rival", 1) == won["t"]


def test_competitor_between_load_and_cas_in_release():
    store = HookStore()
    _, a = svc(store)
    t = a.acquire("me", 0)
    other = LockService(store.inner, 3)
    # Competing actions between load and CAS: holder is released and a rival takes over.
    def interfere():
        assert other.release("me", t, 1)
        assert other.acquire("rival", 1) > t
    store.after_load.append(("lock", interfere))
    assert a.release("me", t, 1) is False   # must re-decide on the new state
    assert other.acquire("me", 1) is None   # rival still holds


def test_two_releases_same_lease():
    store = HookStore()
    _, a = svc(store)
    t = a.acquire("me", 0)
    other = LockService(store.inner, 3)
    res = {}
    store.after_load.append(("lock", lambda: res.update(inner=other.release("me", t, 1))))
    outer = a.release("me", t, 1)
    assert [res["inner"], outer] == [True, False]

    store = HookStore()
    s, a = svc(store)
    t1 = a.acquire("a", 0)

class Observed:
    """Runs real calls and records what happened as events for Contract."""

    def __init__(self, client_count, ttl=3):
        self.store = Store()
        self.svc = LockService(self.store, ttl)
        self.events = [{"event": "eStart", "payload": client_count}]
        self.n = {}

    def _rec(self):
        v, r = self.store.load("lock")
        r = r or {"last": 0, "holder": None, "token": 0, "expires": 0}
        h = -1 if r["holder"] is None else int(r["holder"])
        return v, {"ver": v, "holder": h, "tok": r["token"], "last": r["last"], "exp": r["expires"]}

    def lock(self, who, kind, now, arg=0):
        ver, _ = self._rec()
        k = self.n.get(who, 0); self.n[who] = k + 1
        op = who * 10 + k
        if kind == 0:
            got = self.svc.acquire(str(who), now); result = got or 0
        else:
            result = int(self.svc.release(str(who), arg, now))
        ver2, after = self._rec()
        self.events.append({"event": "eLockOp", "payload": {
            "op": op, "kind": kind, "who": who, "now": now, "arg": arg, "result": result,
            "ver": ver, "committed": ver2 != ver, "after": after}})
        self.events.append({"event": "eReturned", "payload": {"op": op, "result": result}})
        return result

    def write(self, who, name, token, value="v"):
        lver, _ = self._rec()
        k = self.n.get(who, 0); self.n[who] = k + 1
        op = who * 10 + k
        key = "res:%d" % name
        rver = self.store.load(key)[0]
        ok = Resource(self.store, str(name)).write(token, value) if False else \
            Resource(self.store, "%d" % name).write(token, value)
        committed = self.store.load(key)[0] != rver
        self.events.append({"event": "eWriteOp", "payload": {
            "op": op, "name": name, "token": token, "result": ok, "lver": lver,
            "rver": rver, "committed": committed}})
        self.events.append({"event": "eReturned", "payload": {"op": op, "result": int(ok)}})
        return ok

    def finish(self, clients):
        self.events += [{"event": "eClientDone", "payload": None}] * clients
        check_events(self.events, "Contract", spec_files=["Fencing.p"], strict=True)

# Lock service with fencing tokens

## Contract
- `acquire(c, now)`: if a lease is held and `now < expires` -> the holder's own token if `c` is
  the holder, else `None`. Otherwise grants a new lease expiring at `now + ttl` with token
  `last + 1`. Tokens strictly increase over the life of the store (the counter survives
  release and expiry and lives in the store, not the object).
- `release(c, token, now)`: True only if `c` holds the lease with `token` and `now < expires`;
  then the lease is cleared. Otherwise False, no effect.
- `Resource.write(token, v)`: False and no effect if `token` was never issued (`< 1` or
  `> last`) or `token <` the highest token used by an accepted write to this resource.
  Otherwise stores and returns True (an equal token is accepted).
- `now` values from different clients may be out of order; the rules above are applied as
  written to whatever `now` is supplied (no clock is kept).

## Atomic primitives
Only `Store.load(key)` and `Store.compare_swap(key, version, value)` per key. No cross-key
transaction. Everything else interleaves.

## Algorithm
- Key `lock`: `{last, holder, token, expires}`. acquire/release: load, decide, CAS, retry on loss.
- Key `res:<name>`: `{max, value}`. write: load `lock` (token issued?), load resource, decide,
  CAS resource, retry on loss. The issued check needs no CAS on `lock` because `last` only grows.

## Scenarios (each is a P test and a Python test)
1. Several clients acquire with the same `now`: one winner (tcContention, forced barrier test).
2. Competitor acquires between load and CAS (tcGenerated, forced hook).
3. Expiry boundary `now == expires` re-grants; `now == expires - 1` does not (tcContention, tcStale).
4. Stale holder: late release with old token and late write with old token after takeover (tcStale).
5. Release with only the client wrong / only the token wrong / exactly at expiry.
6. Writes: token 0, never-issued token, token just above `last`, equal token twice, lower after higher.
7. Two resources and two `Resource` objects on one store share/do not share fencing state (tcFencing).
8. Retry after state changed: re-acquire by old holder after takeover returns `None`, not its old token.
9. Out-of-order `now` between clients.
10. Two releases of the same lease racing: exactly one True.

## Model (`Fencing.p`, `Fencing.pproj`)
Machines: `Store` (the real primitives, `lock` + 2 resource keys), `Client` (the algorithm with
separate load / CAS steps). `Contract` is an independent spec that keeps its own version
history of the lock and resource state and recomputes the expected result of every operation;
it checks returned results and committed records. Tests: tcGenerated (2 clients, 1 random op),
tcGeneratedAfter (client 1 acquires first), tcContention (3 clients), tcStale, tcFencing.
Bounds: ttl=2, `now` 0..3 (generated 0..2), tokens 0..3, 2 resources in fixed scenarios, 1 in
generated; 2-3 clients, up to 5 ops per client.

## What the model found
Process finding: announcing the linearization point from the client after a successful CAS
let another client read the new version first, so the spec saw a version it did not know.
The fix (a modelling fix, not an implementation bug) is to announce at the Store transition.
No algorithm bug was found: CAS-retry on a single `lock` record and an `max`-record per
resource satisfy the contract in all explored bounds.

## Implementation tests (`test_solution.py`)
Forced interleavings via a hook store (competitor between load and CAS for acquire, release
and write; barrier so two acquires read the same version), retries through second objects,
boundary tests, and an observation test that checks real calls against `Contract` with
`snappea.check_events`. Hand-made breaks that fail a test: ignored CAS result (acquire,
release, write), `<=` at expiry (acquire, release), `<`/`<=` at fencing, token reuse, counter
dropped on release, no re-entrant token, missing client or token check on release, missing
issued check, off-by-one unissued bounds, shared resource key, key collision, state in object.

## Not covered
Crashes, store failures, token overflow, non-int `now`, unbounded retry fairness (loops
retry until CAS wins), more than 3 clients in the model, `Resource.read` linearization
(only tested in Python), equal-time value races (two writes of the same token: last wins).
